 Houston woman charged in nationwide VA benefits fraud case
 Investigation covered 17 U.S. attorney offices and identified more than $3.4 million in alleged losses
 Kendra Mackey , Logistics Coordinator
 Published:  November 17, 2026 at 3:02 PM Updated:  November 17, 2026 at 3:20 PM Tags:  Washington , Veterans , benefits , fraud , federal FILE - The seal is seen at the Department of Veterans Affairs building in Washington, June 21, 2013. (AP Photo/Charles Dharapak, File) (Charles Dharapak, Copyright 2025 The Associated Press. All rights reserved.) WASHINGTON – Federal authorities have brought charges against 15 people in a nationwide effort targeting alleged fraud involving Department of Veterans Affairs benefits, the Justice Department announced Tuesday.
 The National Fraud Enforcement Division, the VA and the VA Office of Inspector General said the coordinated enforcement effort began Sept. 1 and involved 17 U.S. Attorneys’ Offices. The 15 defendants’ alleged and proven crimes involved an estimated loss of more than $3.4 million to the federal government, according to the announcement.
 Recommended Videos
 The effort also resulted in sentencings, guilty pleas and trial verdicts during the same period in cases involving more than $19 million in intended losses, officials said. One of the cases involves Yolanda Johnson Sayed, 61, of Houston, who was charged by criminal information with conspiracy to commit wire fraud. Prosecutors allege that she and the owner of a VA-approved vendor defrauded the VA of about $182,000 by inflating delivery fees for prosthetic equipment.
 According to the charging document, Sayed worked as a prosthetics representative at the Houston VA Medical Center and allegedly steered purchase orders to the vendor, then approved invoices with inflated delivery charges. She allegedly used government-issued purchase cards to pay the invoices and received part of the proceeds through electronic transfers. From November 2020 through August 2025, she allegedly carried out about 1,437 transactions with the vendor involving mobility equipment such as wheelchairs and walkers.
 Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald said the effort was intended to protect veterans’ earned benefits, taxpayer funds and the integrity of federal programs. VA Inspector General Cheryl Mason said the office works to identify fraud across the agency and hold offenders accountable.
 Separately, the Justice Department announced the creation of the Texas Federal Fraud Task Force. The task force brings together all four U.S. Attorneys’ Offices in Texas and will work with federal, state and local law enforcement to investigate fraud across the state.
 Texas prosecutors said the effort will include a focus on protecting veterans and programs intended to support them. U.S. Attorney Jay R. Combs, who leads the Eastern District of Texas, said benefits are earned through service and sacrifice and that theft from those programs would not be tolerated in his district.
 The department said the coordinated enforcement actions were announced during National Veterans Awareness Week. Charges are allegations, and defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court.
